subject: Front Line of Fresh Barbershop Profile
overview: Host Danielle Balocca interviewed Donald Morton, owner of Front Line of Fresh in West Medford, regarding his professional background and business philosophy. The discussion focused on the shop's commitment to diversity, its role in the historically Black neighborhood of West Medford, and the challenges of entrepreneurship.

items.title: Historical context and introduction
items.summary: Host Danielle Balocca provides historical background on West Medford's Black-owned salons and the Afro-American Remembrance Project before introducing barber Donald Morton.

items.title: Personal background and favorite local dining
items.summary: Donald Morton introduces himself as a Somerville native and professional barber, identifying Semolina Kitchen & Bar as a favorite local restaurant.

items.title: Business origins and professional path
items.summary: Morton describes his decision to enter barber school to achieve independence after working jobs with management structures he found restrictive.

items.title: Business management and financial realities
items.summary: Morton discusses the complexities of managing a business, supporting independent contractors, and navigating the significant financial overhead required to open a shop.

items.title: Naming and branding of Front Line of Fresh
items.summary: Morton explains the military-inspired origins of his business name and the creation of his 'Barack the Barber' professional persona.

items.title: Commitment to diversity and inclusivity
items.summary: The discussion highlights the intentional diversity of the shop's staff and the goal of creating a comfortable, all-inclusive environment for all clients.

items.title: West Medford neighborhood history
items.summary: Morton and Balocca discuss the history of West Medford as a Black neighborhood and the importance of representation among modern local business owners.

items.title: Services, client experience, and community engagement
items.summary: Morton details the grooming services provided and expresses a desire to host community events like sports tournaments to bring people together.

items.title: Professional training and industry habits
items.summary: Morton discusses the limitations of barber school and his focus on mentoring new barbers to develop proper technical and social habits.

items.title: Entrepreneurial advice and local outlook
items.summary: The interview concludes with advice for aspiring business owners and anticipation for new developments in the square, such as the Medford Brewing Company.
